facts.claim: Issue #26207 'Pivot operations not partitionable causing performance regression' exists in pola-rs/polars, labelled regression, opened 2026-01-21, closed as completed 2026-08-10

Regression reported starting v1.36.1; pivot unified with group-by using filtered aggregations that were not treated as partitionable (about 680 ms on v1.35.2 vs 35.6 s on v1.37.1 in reporter's example)
The fix PR is #28749 'fix: Correct partitionable filter handling for pivot', MERGED 2026-08-10. The row says the PR was not found, so the row is wrong: the fix is public in the repo's git history
Closed-unmerged PR #28736 'support AExpr::Filter in can_pre_agg for partitioned pivot execution' is an earlier attempt and also public
The fix has no maintainer comment describing it on the issue; the root cause write-up came from an external contributor
Licence MIT (taken from GitHub API spdx field; not separately re-checked)
Rust build of the polars workspace finishes offline within the budget (smoke_build is empty, so no build evidence)

v1.kill_reason: One lever. The regression is one predicate (Filter in can_pre_agg for partitioned pivot), the upstream fix is merged public history in PR #28749, and the seed's own band note says a frontier agent finds the planner change easily. The remaining work is correctness checks on edge aggregations, which does not fill an 8 h tier. The seed's claim that the PR was not found is contradicted by the repo. Build cost is also unmeasured (smoke_build empty), so K12 is a secondary risk.

Build.why: Full workspace build time unmeasured and probably days-scale

spike_plan.kill_if: Build exceeds about 3 h or 16 GB; or the fix is a trivial predicate change with the speedup already reached by an obvious edit (confirms K10)
spike_plan.pass_if: Build finishes within about 2 h on 8 cores; base outputs match the fixed build on all differential cases; the fix gives a clear median speedup on tall pivots
steps: Clone pola-rs/polars in a throwaway container with network; check out the parent of PR #28749 (the regressed base) and confirm the diff of #28749 is small
Build the Python extension or the needed crates at the base (record build wall-clock, peak RAM, and whether it fits in 16 GB)
Write a differential script: pivot on random schemas (types, nulls, mean/sum/first/last/count, ordering), comparing base against the #28749 build
Run timed wide and tall pivots on base and fixed builds (5 runs each, median) to measure the speedup
Check determinism: rerun the same seed twice and compare outputs byte-for-byte

v1.summary: The regression is real (polars issue #26207, regression label, closed 2026-08-10), but the seed's claim that no fix PR exists is wrong: fix PR #28749 is merged in the public history. Because the fix is a single planner predicate that a frontier agent can find from the issue text, the task is one-lever and too easy for an 8 h tier, so I kill it as K10 (with a secondary K12 build-cost risk, since smoke_build did not run).
